{

  "stream": true,

  "tools": [...]                       # forwarded when you configure Tools on the agent
}

When you add tools on the agent's "Tools" step we forward them in
the OpenAI `tools` shape. Your model — and your serving framework —
must support function calling for it to fire. Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp
server, LM Studio all do for chat-tuned models.

tool's endpoint and feed the JSON response back as a tool message,
exactly like the hosted providers.

configFields.help: Lets the agent add a natural sound where one fits — a laugh, a sigh, or a beat of pause — and soften or quicken a line to suit what it is saying. Grok has no emotion setting, so the second part is pacing rather than tone. No change to cost. Lines the agent paces are sent over a slightly slower connection, so expect a little more delay on those.
configFields.label: Expression control

tts.name: xAI (Grok)

tts.blurb: Soniox real-time TTS — 60+ languages with one voice speaking them all (strong Hindi + code-switching), plus instant cross-lingual voice cloning; μ-law 8k telephony, 24k HD on web, gapless streaming. Uses the same key as Soniox STT.

configFields.help: Soniox needs the spoken language set explicitly — one voice speaks all 60+. Mixed scripts within a turn still work.
configFields.label: Language

configFields.help: Speaking pace. 1.0 is natural; below 1 is slower, above 1 is faster.
configFields.label: Speed

configFields.help: Shorten pauses for snappier conversational turns (tts-rt-v2).
configFields.label: Reduce silence between sentences

configFields.help: Lets the agent colour how a line is delivered — calm, apologetic, warm. No change to cost or latency.
configFields.label: Expression control

tts.name: Soniox

tts.blurb: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS — 30 voices that each speak 90+ languages, directed in plain English: you write the speaker, the scene and the accent (Indian, American, British…) and the same voice performs it. With expression on, the model steers its own delivery inline — [whispers], [laughs], [excited] — clause by clause. Synthesised one whole turn at a time so the performance never drifts between clauses. μ-law 8k telephony, 24k HD on web. Uses the same key as the Gemini LLM.

configFields.help: 3.1 Flash is the only Gemini TTS model that streams — the 2.5 models synthesise the whole turn before the first frame plays, so keep them for cached openers, not live turns.
configFields.label: Model

options.label: Gemini 2.5 Pro TTS (no streaming, higher quality)

configFields.help: Lets the model direct its own delivery inline — [whispers], [laughs], [sighs], [excited], [curious] and anything else descriptive — on top of the standing brief below. On by default here because this engine performs bracketed direction natively rather than reading it aloud; it still needs the platform SPEECH_TAGS flag to be on.
configFields.label: Expression tags

configFields.help: The speaker, as you would brief an actor. e.g. "A 32-year-old customer-support lead at an Indian fintech. Patient, never salesy, speaks like a competent colleague." Leave blank to let the voice speak plainly.
configFields.label: Audio profile — who is speaking

configFields.help: The situation and the vibe. e.g. "An inbound support call. The caller is mildly frustrated about a failed payment and wants it resolved in one call." Gemini performs the scene, so changing it changes the delivery.
configFields.label: Scene — where this is happening

configFields.help: Pacing, emphasis, delivery. e.g. "Unhurried. Land the account number clearly, one digit group at a time. Never sound chirpy about a failure."
configFields.label: Director's notes — how to deliver it

configFields.help: Any voice can speak any accent — this is where you choose it. Be specific: "Indian English, neutral urban", "Indian English with a light Tamil lilt", "American English, west-coast", "British English, RP". Blank = whatever the voice and language imply.
configFields.label: Accent

configFields.help: Gemini detects the language from the words it is given, so this is only needed when the text alone is ambiguous — romanised Hindi, or a digits-only utterance.
configFields.label: Language

tts.blurb: Point at any streaming-HTTP TTS endpoint. Describe the request body + audio format once; we reframe the audio to telephony μ-law. MVP: streaming HTTP (mulaw / pcm16 / mp3).

configFields.help: Passed through as {model} in the request template.
configFields.label: Model (optional)

configFields.help: Maps your synth request + audio response to our contract — see the reference below. Set your endpoint key in the “Bring your own key” field above (required — referenced as {apiKey}, billed as BYOK). Steer your endpoint to raw mulaw/pcm to skip an ffmpeg pass. wire_codec is REQUIRED.
configFields.label: Vendor descriptor (JSON)

docs.intro: We POST your request_template (with {text}/{voice}/{apiKey} filled in) to your endpoint over an SSRF-guarded https client, then reframe the streamed audio to μ-law 8k 20 ms telephony frames based on your declared wire_codec. mulaw_8k passes through; pcm16_* and mp3 are transcoded.

sections.label: Example — a raw-μ-law streaming HTTP vendor

tts.name: Custom TTS (bring your own endpoint)

tts.name: UnrealSpeech

tts.blurb: Gnani Timbre v2.5 — 42 voices for 10 Indian languages plus Hinglish, and zero-shot voice cloning from a 5–30 s sample. Streams over a WebSocket (first audio about 0.2 s on a warm socket); μ-law 8k on phone calls, 24k HD on web. Speed is the only delivery control — no expression tags. A cloned voice is synthesised a whole sentence at a time, so it starts a second or more later; while several Gnani keys rotate, cloning on the platform key is paused. Uses the same key as Gnani STT.

configFields.help: Timbre v2.5 is the model Gnani serves for its voices. A cloned voice is synthesised on Gnani's clone model automatically.
configFields.label: Model

configFields.help: Auto detects the language from the script of each sentence (Gnani's recommendation for mixed content). Each voice is tuned for one language — pick it to match the voice for the best pronunciation of numbers and names.
configFields.label: Language

configFields.help: Speaking pace — Gnani accepts 0.85 to 1.15; 1.0 is natural. Gnani has no other delivery control (no expression tags). Cloned voices ignore it.
configFields.label: Speed
